notes: USMLE Content Outline (2026) includes hypocoagulable fibrinogen disorders in the Blood & Lymphoreticular System.

The NLM-indexed 2021 review on congenital afibrinogenemia/hypofibrinogenemia directly documents extremely prolonged PT, aPTT and thrombin time with undetectable fibrinogen activity and antigen in afibrinogenemia.

exact_locator_notes: USMLE Content Outline (2026), Blood & Lymphoreticular System, page 5 — Coagulation disorders, hypocoagulable — hypofibrinogenemia.
Congenital Afibrinogenemia and Hypofibrinogenemia… (Diagnostics 2021): Laboratory Assays; Table 2 — Diagnostic procedures of quantitative fibrinogen disorders.

blueprint.competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
blueprint.competency_task: Selects the most likely diagnosis from history and coagulation studies.

difficulty.rationale: Requires integration of discriminating clinical clues with a mechanism or diagnosis rather than isolated fact recall.

option_audit.correct: The quantitative absence of fibrinogen plus fibrin-dependent assay prolongation is diagnostic.
option_audit.hemophilia_A: Would primarily prolong aPTT with normal fibrinogen and PT.
option_audit.factor_XIII: Can cause delayed/umbilical bleeding but routine PT/aPTT/TT are not prolonged because fibrin formation precedes factor XIII cross-linking.
option_audit.vWD: Does not cause absent fibrinogen antigen and generally does not produce marked PT/TT prolongation.
option_audit.dysfibrinogenemia: A qualitative defect ordinarily leaves measurable antigen rather than complete absence of both antigen and activity.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Umbilical stump bleeding with normal platelets, markedly prolonged PT/aPTT/TT, and complete absence of both fibrinogen activity and antigen uniquely supports congenital afibrinogenemia.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Factor XIII deficiency is a strong clinical mimic because it can cause umbilical stump bleeding, but routine PT/aPTT/TT assess clot formation before factor XIII cross-linking and are typically normal; here every fibrin-dependent assay is markedly prolonged.
adversarial_second_pass.dysfibrinogenemia_attack: Dysfibrinogenemia is qualitative: functional fibrinogen is disproportionately low relative to antigen. Undetectable activity together with undetectable antigen supports afibrinogenemia.
adversarial_second_pass.hemophilia_vwd_attack: Hemophilia A causes an isolated aPTT abnormality; von Willebrand disease does not eliminate circulating fibrinogen and does not produce this pan-assay pattern.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No numerical coagulation cutoff, prevalence, inheritance probability or treatment dose is asserted.
